---
name: hub-docs-governance
description: Set up, migrate, index, audit, or synchronize Git-native project docs for software, ML research, and agent harnesses. Use for docs/ initialization, AGENTS.md navigation, stale documentation, PR/release checks, ID integrity, or changes to implemented-state references.
---

# Documentation Governance

**Scope:** Maintain the documentation system and its **living** truth. For a new FEAT/RFC/DES/ADR use `hub-design-decision-management`; for EXP/EVAL use `hub-experiment-evaluation`.

## Canonical layout (create only needed paths)

```text
README.md
AGENTS.md                         # optional agent instructions
docs/README.md                    # index and conventions
docs/architecture/                # implemented behavior: living
docs/reference/                   # API and interfaces: living
docs/features/                    # FEAT-0001-slug.md
docs/proposals/                   # RFC-0001-slug.md
docs/designs/                     # DES-0001-slug/{README.md,v1.md,v2.md}
docs/decisions/                   # ADR-0001-slug.md
docs/experiments/                 # EXP-0001-slug/{plan.md,results.md}
docs/evaluations/                 # EVAL-0001-slug.md
```

## Shared rules

- Git + Markdown are canonical for narrative technical records. External issue trackers own tasks; experiment trackers own raw run metrics/artifacts; link them instead of duplicating.
- IDs are **project-local and unique**: `FEAT`, `RFC`, `DES`, `ADR`, `EXP`, `EVAL` with four-digit numeric suffixes. Never recycle IDs. `DES-0001@v2` resolves to the corresponding `v2.md`.
- Substantive records use YAML frontmatter `id`, `title`, `status`, `created`, `updated` (ISO date); designs also have integer `version`. Link `related` IDs and real URLs where available.
- **Code/tests/deployment evidence** determine what is implemented/released. Proposed, accepted/selected, implemented, and released are distinct.
- Living docs reflect verified current behavior; historical RFCs, ADRs, major design snapshots, and experiment evidence are preserved. Correct historical factual errors explicitly; do not silently change prior rationale or results.
- Small copy changes use Git diffs. Major design alternatives receive a new snapshot; reversed decisions receive new superseding ADRs.

## Initialize or migrate

1. Inspect repository `README`, existing `AGENTS.md`, docs, code/tests, and authoritative external trackers. **Respect existing conventions** where possible; avoid duplication or wholesale renaming.
2. Create/update `docs/README.md`: current architecture link + compact `ID | Title | Type | Status | Related` index. Only link real files.
3. Add a root README link to docs; add/merge an `AGENTS.md` entry point *if agents will use the repo*. Tell agents to read docs index, current architecture, and relevant records before editing.
4. Allocate unused IDs after inspecting existing files; migrate with explicit old→new pointers and preserved Git history.
5. Create only necessary paths. Do not invent implementation details, metric results, or fake project-specific examples.

**Minimal index:**

```markdown
# Project documentation
- Current implementation: [Architecture](architecture/overview.md)
- Historical decisions: [ADRs](decisions/)

| ID | Record | Status | Related |
|---|---|---|---|
| DES-0001 | [Execution design](designs/DES-0001-execution/README.md) | proposed | RFC-0001 |
```

The row above is illustrative; emit it only if the referenced files exist.

## Sync / audit workflow (on PR, release, or when drift suspected)

1. Inspect `docs/README.md`, affected living docs, feature specs, design/decision links, code/tests and available release evidence.
2. Validate unique IDs, valid frontmatter, resolvable relative links, version indices, and supersession pointers.
3. Compare **documented vs verified** feature behavior, architecture, API, and release status. Never infer shipped state from an accepted RFC or selected design.
4. Verify traceability when relevant: FEAT/RFC → DES → EXP/EVAL → ADR → PR/tests/release. **Do not require every node for every change.**
5. Patch outdated living docs and necessary indexes **in the same PR** as implementation when feasible. Preserve historical text; create a new design version/ADR for substantive changes.
6. Check release notes (`CHANGELOG.md`, if used) and feature release references.
7. Report `verified / issues / changes applied / unable to verify`, with paths and evidence. Do not claim to have tested or deployed anything you have not.

## Exit criteria

- Navigation links work; no duplicate IDs; documented status matches available evidence.
- Historical designs, rejected alternatives and negative experiments remain discoverable.
- List changed files and remaining uncertainties; do not issue a false all-clear when evidence is missing.
